_meta.purpose: 本会话高频 18 个工具描述的精简版，用于 product.json prompts 覆盖
_meta.rules: 保留硬约束/失败条件/平台差异/必做前置/触发条件；删除重复强调、冗长解释、冗余示例

prompts.name: tool-read-description
prompts.template:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.
- file_path must be absolute. Assume any path the User gives is valid; a nonexistent file returns an error.
- Reads up to 2000 lines from the start by default; optional offset/limit for long files. A full read is preferred over a partial one.
- Lines longer than 2000 chars are truncated. Output is cat -n style, numbered from 1.
- Images are not returned: the tool yields the file's path and tells you to use ViewImage.
- Also reads .ipynb, returning all cells with their outputs.
- Files only, not directories (use `ls` via Bash for a directory).
- Speculative parallel reads are encouraged. You will often be asked to read screenshots — use ViewImage with the given absolute path.
- An empty file comes back as a system reminder instead of content.

prompts.name: tool-viewimage-description
prompts.template:
Inspect an image file. Multimodal models receive the image itself; otherwise a vision model reads it and returns a text answer.
- image_path: absolute path, .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.gif/.bmp.
- query must be self-contained — the vision model sees ONLY the image and your query, never this conversation. State exactly what to extract, e.g. "in this login screenshot, list misaligned or overlapping elements".
- Treat the returned text as the whole answer: do not infer details it omits. If the answer is ambiguous, re-ask with a narrower query instead of guessing.
- Does not edit or generate images.

prompts.name: tool-write-description
prompts.template:
Writes a file, overwriting any existing file at that path.
- An existing file MUST be read with Read first, or this tool fails.
- Prefer Edit on existing files; create new files only when required.
- Never create docs (*.md, README) proactively — only when explicitly requested.
- No emojis unless the user asks.

prompts.name: tool-edit-description
prompts.template:
Exact string replacement in a file. Matches `old_string` against the file on disk directly — a prior Read is not required; on mismatch, re-read and retry.
- Preserve exact indentation as it appears AFTER the line-number prefix (`  <n>\t`). Never include the prefix in old_string or new_string.
- Fails if `old_string` is not unique — add surrounding context, or use `replace_all` (also the way to rename a variable across a file).
- Fails if `old_string` is missing, differs in whitespace, or equals `new_string`.
- Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones; no emojis unless asked.
- Never use this tool to "verify" content or as a no-op.

prompts.name: tool-glob-description
prompts.template:
- Fast file pattern matching at any codebase size
- Glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"; returns paths sorted by modification time
- Pagination: `limit` (default 100), `offset` (default 0)
- Use for finding files by name; for open-ended multi-round searching use the Agent tool instead
- Parallel speculative searches are encouraged

prompts.name: tool-grep-description
prompts.template:
Search file contents with ripgrep.
- ALWAYS use this instead of `grep`/`rg` in Bash — it handles permissions and access correctly.
- Full regex. Literal braces need escaping (`interface\{\}`). Use `multiline: true` for cross-line patterns like `struct \{[\s\S]*?field`.
- Filter with `glob` (`*.js`, `**/*.tsx`) or `type` (`js`, `py`, `rust`).
- `output_mode`: `content` (matching lines), `files_with_matches` (paths, default), `count`.
- Paginate with `head_limit` (default unlimited) and `offset`.
- For open-ended multi-round searching use the Agent tool.

prompts.name: tool-bash-description
prompts.template:
Runs a shell command. Working directory persists between calls; shell state (variables, functions, aliases) does not. Environment comes from the user profile.
IMPORTANT: the user's default shell is {{defaultShell}} — write syntax for that shell.
{% if platform == 'win32' %}IMPORTANT: on Windows this is Git Bash (POSIX sh, not cmd.exe): forward slashes, drive paths like `/c/Users/name/`, `/dev/null` (not `NUL`/`2>nul`), `$VAR` (not `%VAR%`). Use the PowerShell tool for Windows-only work (registry, services, COM, .NET) instead of calling powershell/pwsh from here.{% endif %}
Use for terminal work (git, package managers, builds, tests, programs). When a dedicated tool exists, use it:
- Read / Edit / Write (not cat, head, sed, echo >)
- Glob (not find/ls) · Grep (not grep/rg)
- Communicate by outputting text (not echo/printf)
Rules:
- Verify the parent directory exists before creating files. Quote paths with spaces.
- Keep the working directory: use absolute paths instead of `cd`, and never prefix `cd <cwd>` (especially for git) — it is redundant and triggers a permission prompt.
- `timeout`: default {{bashDefaultTimeoutMs}}ms, max {{bashMaxTimeoutMs}}ms (env `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`). Omit it for long commands; set it only with a known upper bound.
- Long-running work: `run_in_background: true` → task_id plus a `<task-notification>` on finish. Do not poll or sleep; use TaskOutput when you need output, TaskStop to stop. A foreground command that hits its timeout is auto-backgrounded (except `sleep`).
- Never detach with nohup/setsid/disown/`&` — they escape task management and may be killed on exit. In `-p` runs the process dies when the turn ends, so collect background results before finishing.
- Avoid `sleep`; never retry a failing command in a sleep loop — diagnose the cause. To wait on an external process use a check command.
- Independent commands → parallel calls; dependent → `&&`. Use `;` only when earlier failures don't matter. No newline-separated commands.
- Non-interactive: never use interactive flags (`git rebase -i`, `git add -i`/`-p`) or anything that waits for input.
- A denied command is final: do not retry it or an equivalent elsewhere; report what was blocked. The only escalation path is `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` after a sandbox policy failure.
- Git: prefer new commits over `--amend`; consider safer alternatives before `reset --hard` / `push --force` / `checkout --`; never skip hooks (`--no-verify`) or signing unless asked — fix the hook instead. Use `/commit` or `/commit-push-pr`, and `gh` for GitHub URLs, issues, PRs and checks.

prompts.name: tool-powershell-description
prompts.template:
Runs a PowerShell command on Windows. Working directory persists between calls; shell state (variables, functions) does not.
Use for Windows terminal work (git, npm, docker, cmdlets) and Windows-only tasks (registry, services, COM, .NET). When a dedicated tool exists, use it:
- Read / Edit / Write (not Get-Content, Set-Content/Out-File)
- Glob (not Get-ChildItem -Recurse) · Grep (not Select-String)
- Communicate by outputting text (not Write-Output/Write-Host)
Never start `bash`, `sh` or `wsl` from PowerShell to get around tool boundaries.
{% if psEdition == 'desktop' %}Edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
- No `&&`/`||` (parser error). Chain: `A; if ($?) { B }`; unconditional: `A; B`.
- No `?:`, `??`, `?.`; use if/else and `$null -eq` checks.
- Avoid `2>&1` on native executables — it sets `$?` to false even on exit code 0.
- Default file encoding is UTF-16 LE; pass `-Encoding utf8` when writing files other tools read.
{% elif psEdition == 'core' %}Edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh). `&&`, `||`, `?:`, `??`, `?.` available; default encoding UTF-8 without BOM.
{% else %}Edition unknown: assume Windows PowerShell 5.1 and avoid `&&`, `||`, `?:`, `??`, `?.`.
{% endif %}
Syntax: escape char is backtick (`), not backslash; single quotes are literal. Registry paths use PSDrives (`HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...`), not `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`. Env vars: read `$env:NAME`, set `$env:NAME = "value"`. Run an executable whose path has spaces with the call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\..."`. Quote paths with spaces.
- Pass multiline strings to native executables with a single-quoted here-string (no `$`/backtick expansion); the closing `'@` must start at column 0: `git commit -m @'` … `'@`.
- The working directory is already the project directory; do not prefix commands with `cd`/`Set-Location`. Verify the parent directory exists before creating files.
Usage notes:
- `timeout`: default 120000ms, max 600000ms.
- Long-running work: `run_in_background: true` → task_id plus a `<task-notification>` on finish; do not poll or `Start-Sleep`; use TaskOutput when you need output, TaskStop to stop. A foreground command that hits its timeout is auto-backgrounded (except `Start-Sleep`). Do not emulate background tasks with `Start-Job` or detached processes.
- Independent commands → parallel calls in one message; dependent → chain per the edition rules above.
- Non-interactive: never use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, `pause`, or editor-opening commands (`git rebase -i`, `git add -i`). Add `-Confirm:$false` to destructive cmdlets you intend to run (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`), `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
- Git: prefer new commits over `--amend`; never skip hooks (`--no-verify`) unless asked.
- A denied command is final: do not retry it or an equivalent elsewhere; report what was blocked.

prompts.name: tool-taskcreate-description
prompts.template:
Create tasks to track multi-step work in this session.
Use when: 3+ distinct steps, non-trivial planning, plan mode, the user asks for a list, the user hands over several tasks, or after receiving new instructions. Skip for a single trivial step or pure conversation — just do the work.
Fields:
- subject: imperative title ("Fix auth bug in login flow")
- description: what to do, context, acceptance criteria
- activeForm: present continuous, shown while in_progress ("Fixing auth bug")
Workflow: capture requirements as tasks on arrival, set in_progress before starting, completed the moment it is done, and add follow-ups found along the way. Keep items specific and small-grained; TaskList after creating to verify.

prompts.name: tool-taskget-description
prompts.template:
Fetch one task by ID for its full description and dependencies. Use before starting work on an assigned task, and to see what blocks it or what it blocks.
Returns subject, description, status ('pending' | 'in_progress' | 'completed'), blocks (tasks waiting on this), blockedBy (tasks that must finish first).
Check that blockedBy is empty before starting; use TaskList for the summary view.

prompts.name: tool-taskupdate-description
prompts.template:
Update a task.
Complete it only when fully done — never with failing tests, partial work, unresolved errors, or missing dependencies. If blocked, keep it in_progress and create a task describing the blocker. After resolving, call TaskList for the next item. `status: deleted` removes a task permanently (also for tasks created in error or no longer relevant).
Fields: status, subject, description, activeForm, owner, metadata (null deletes a key), addBlocks, addBlockedBy.
Status flow: pending → in_progress → completed.
Read the latest state with TaskGet before updating.

prompts.name: tool-taskoutput-description
prompts.template:
- Retrieve output from a running or completed task (background shell, agent, remote session) by task_id, with status information
- `block: true` (default) waits for completion; `false` checks current status
- Task IDs come from the task list

prompts.name: tool-tasklist-description
tool-sendmessage-description
prompts.template:
Send messages to agent teammates and answer protocol requests.
Types:
- `message` — DM one teammate. Fields: recipient, content, summary (5–10 words, shown as the UI preview). A teammate's plain text is NOT visible to the lead or to others: to communicate you MUST call this tool — acknowledging in text does nothing.
- `broadcast` — the same message to everyone, one delivery per teammate, cost scaling with team size. Only for stop-work signals or announcements that genuinely affect every teammate; default to `message`.
- `shutdown_request` — recipient, content. The teammate approves (exits) or rejects with a reason.
- `shutdown_response` — request_id (copy the incoming `requestId`), approve: true|false, optional content. You must call the tool; saying "I'll shut down" is not enough.
- `plan_approval_response` — request_id, recipient, approve, optional content. Approval makes a plan_mode teammate exit plan mode and start work; rejection carries your feedback so it can revise.
Notes:
- Incoming teammate messages are delivered automatically — never poll an inbox. Reporting on them needs no quote; they are already rendered to the user.
- Always refer to teammates by name ("team-lead", "researcher"), never by UUID.
- Do not send structured JSON status messages — mark tasks with TaskUpdate and the system notifies when you stop.
- A background agent (Agent with `run_in_background: true`) sends results back with `recipient: "main"`; the main agent receives them automatically.

prompts.name: tool-deferexecutetool-description
prompts.template:
Execute a deferred tool by name, using a schema loaded through ToolSearch.
- Load the schema with ToolSearch first; skip it only when you already know the name and parameters.
- Parameters are validated against the schema before execution; normal permission checks and hooks apply.
Example: DeferExecuteTool({ toolName: "ImageGen", params: { prompt: "a sunset over mountains" } })
On validation failure the error includes the expected schema.

prompts.name: tool-toolsearch-description
prompts.template:
Load the schema of deferred tools.
Deferred tools are NOT directly callable — ToolSearch to load the schema, then DeferExecuteTool to run.
- Exact (preferred): `tool_names: ["ImageGen"]` — use when you know the tool name.
- Search: `queries: ["image generation"]` — use when unsure which tool fits.
Never guess parameters without loading the schema first.
The deferred tools available this session; their schemas are NOT loaded and calling them directly fails with InputValidationError:
{% if toolSearchDeferredTools %}
<available_deferred_tools>
{{toolSearchDeferredTools}}
</available_deferred_tools>
{% endif %}
